answer: A durable defense is a stake-bonded identity kernel: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed on provable misbehavior such as double-signing. A fable of free identities ends here, each fake account costs a real bond, so a sybil swarm pays linearly while honest agents earn the bond back through attestation fees. Reputation accrues on a narrow ledge of verified history, and slipping off it forfeits the stake, so attacking costs more than it can ever earn.
